spotlight.label: Spotlight
spotlight.title: COP31 in Antalya
spotlight.intro: Bangladesh wants adaptation finance tripled and paid as grants, not loans, plus real money for loss and damage. Devlens follows what the summit means for the sector until the talks close.

today.text: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman gave Bangladesh's national statement, asking that at least half of all climate finance go to adaptation, as grants, with debt relief and a just transition mechanism. UN Climate Change launched its Net-Zero Recognition Framework for companies, cities and other non-state actors, and leaders met on methane. On Wednesday, Guterres told the leaders' summit emissions must fall about 6% a year; current plans deliver at best a third of that.

watch: Adaptation finance: whether a draft text sets a baseline or share for adaptation money, after Bangladesh asked for at least 50%.
Just transition: whether the Belém-Antalya Action Mechanism is adopted.
Finance on the agenda: developing countries want tripling adaptation finance discussed; developed countries are resisting, and an EU official has warned of no political will for new pledges.
Gender: UN Women found 73% of countries recognise gender-specific climate risks, but just over one in three address them fully.
